title: Pre-publish health check
content:
## Why run a pre-publish health check?

Before you commit to a production build or submit your mobile app to the App Store or Google Play, it's critical to verify that the app behaves as expected on real devices. A pre-publish health check catches UI glitches, navigation issues, API errors, and performance problems **before** they reach your users—saving you time, EAS build credits, and embarrassment.

Emergent generates a live preview URL for every mobile app. Use it to test thoroughly before you trigger a production build or start the [publishing to the stores](/publishing-to-the-stores) process.

---

## Preview & test the mobile app first

<Info title="Test early, test often">
Your workspace provides an instant preview of the mobile app. Open it on your phone to check layout, navigation, and features—all without burning a build credit or waiting for a compile.
</Info>

Every time the AI agents rebuild your mobile app, Emergent updates the preview. You can:

- Open the preview URL in your browser (desktop or mobile) to see a web-based simulation.
- Scan the QR code with your phone to launch the live app in Expo Go (see below).
- Navigate through every screen, tap buttons, fill forms, and verify API calls.

**What to check:**

- UI renders correctly on both iOS and Android (test on at least one device from each platform if possible).
- Navigation flows work end-to-end (tab bars, drawer menus, deep links).
- Forms validate input and display error messages.
- Images, fonts, and icons load.
- API calls succeed (check network panel or logs if something breaks).
- Push notifications, authentication flows, or third-party SDKs behave as expected.

If you spot a bug, describe it in chat—Emergent's agents will fix the code and regenerate the preview. Repeat until the app is solid.

---

## Local testing & testing on your phone with Expo Go

The fastest way to test your mobile app on a real device is with **Expo Go**, a free companion app that runs Expo projects instantly—no Xcode, no Android Studio, no builds.

<Steps>
<Step title="Install Expo Go on your phone">
Download **Expo Go** from the [App Store](https://apps.apple.com/app/expo-go/id982107779) (iOS) or [Google Play](https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=host.exp.exponent) (Android). It's free and maintained by Expo.
</Step>

<Step title="Open the preview in your workspace">
In the Emergent workspace, locate the mobile app preview panel. You'll see a QR code and a preview URL. See [a tour of the workspace](/a-tour-of-the-workspace) if you need help finding it.
</Step>

<Step title="Scan the QR code">
- **iOS**: Open the Camera app and point it at the QR code. Tap the notification banner that appears.
- **Android**: Open Expo Go and tap **Scan QR Code**, then point your camera at the code.

The app will load and run directly on your device, connected to Emergent's live preview server.
</Step>

<Step title="Iterate and re-test">
Make changes in chat, wait for the agents to rebuild, and the app in Expo Go will **hot-reload automatically**—usually within seconds. You can iterate quickly without leaving your phone.
</Step>
</Steps>

<Tip title="Use Expo Go for all pre-publish testing">
Expo Go gives you a production-like experience on real hardware. Test gestures, animations, keyboard behavior, and camera/location permissions. Only move to a full EAS build once the app is stable.
</Tip>

<Warning title="Expo Go limitations">
Expo Go cannot run apps with custom native code (e.g., certain third-party SDKs or native modules outside the Expo SDK). If your app uses such features, you'll need a development build or a production build via EAS. Most Emergent apps work fine in Expo Go.
</Warning>

---

## EAS price & plan comparison

When you're ready to generate a production build—either for local testing, TestFlight/internal testing, or store submission—you'll use **Expo Application Services (EAS Build)**. EAS is Expo's cloud build infrastructure; Emergent integrates with it to compile your app in the background.

<Note title="Separate from Emergent plans">
EAS pricing is set by Expo, not Emergent. You'll need an Expo account and an EAS subscription (or free tier credits) to trigger builds. See [plans & the free tier](/plans-the-free-tier) for how Emergent's own pricing works.
</Note>

### EAS Build pricing tiers (as of 2024)

The table below compares Expo's EAS Build plans. Visit [expo.dev/pricing](https://expo.dev/pricing) for the latest official pricing.

| Feature | **Free** | **Production** | **Enterprise** |
|---------|----------|----------------|----------------|
| **Price** | $0/month | ~$99/month (per-seat or team pricing) | Custom |
| **Builds per month** | Limited credits (~15–30 depending on platform) | Unlimited | Unlimited |
| **Concurrency** | 1 build at a time | Higher (2–4+ concurrent) | Custom |
| **Build timeout** | Standard | Extended | Custom |
| **Priority queue** | No | Yes | Yes |
| **Support** | Community | Email/chat | Dedicated |
| **Best for** | Prototyping, personal projects, early testing | Production apps, frequent releases | Large teams, compliance, SLA requirements |

**Notes:**

- The **Free** tier gives you enough credits to test the build process and generate a few production APKs/IPAs. Perfect for validating your app before committing to a paid plan.
- **Production** tier is billed per seat or team; check Expo's pricing page for exact numbers (prices vary by region and team size).
- **Enterprise** includes on-premise build workers, audit logs, SSO, and custom SLAs—contact Expo's sales team.

<Tip title="Start with the free tier">
If you're pre-publishing for the first time, use EAS Free to generate a test build. Once you're confident the app is ready and you need frequent builds (e.g., for beta testing or App Store submission), upgrade to Production.
</Tip>

### How builds are triggered in Emergent

When you ask Emergent to "build the mobile app for iOS" or "create an Android APK," the platform:

1. Commits the latest code to your project repository.
2. Runs `eas build` via the EAS CLI, authenticated with your Expo account.
3. Queues the build on Expo's servers (subject to your EAS plan's concurrency and priority).
4. Returns the build URL and artifact (APK or IPA) once complete.

You'll be prompted to connect your Expo account the first time you request a build. See [your first build (walkthrough)](/your-first-build-walkthrough) for step-by-step instructions.
